questions.why: Repeated method signatures in an interface are overloads, so `on('close', (code) => ...)` types `code` as `number`. A mapped event-to-payload type scales better when there are many events.
questions.asked: Node's own typings use this pattern, and typed event emitters are a common exercise.

questions.q: What does each property of `Handlers` accept?
choices: Each handler takes only its own member of `Action`
Every handler takes the full `Action` union
Any string key, each taking an `Action`
Nothing: mapped types can only iterate over keys
questions.why: Since TS 4.1 a mapped type can iterate over any union and pick each key with `as`; each member keeps its own type, so each handler receives its narrowed action. Iterating `Action['type']` instead would lose that link.
questions.asked: Typed handler maps for reducers, events or WebSocket messages are built this way.

questions.q: `types/express.d.ts` contains only `declare module 'express' { interface Request { user?: User } }`, with no imports or exports. What goes wrong?
choices: Nothing; the declaration merges into Express as intended
Only `.ts` files may augment modules, not `.d.ts` files
tsc ignores the file entirely because it has no top-level export
It declares a new ambient `'express'` module that shadows the real types
questions.why: Augmentation only happens inside a module (a file with an import or export). In a script file, `declare module 'express'` is an ambient declaration of the whole module, replacing it. Add `export {}` or an import to make it an augmentation.
questions.asked: This silently breaks Express types in real projects, and diagnosing it shows deep module knowledge.

questions.q: A library's package.json has `"exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/index.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" } }`. Why can consumers get no types?
choices: Conditions match in order, and `import` matches first, so `types` is never reached
`types` must be a top-level field, never inside `exports`
The `.d.ts` file must be named `index.d.mts` when the package is ESM
Consumers must add the package name to their tsconfig `types` array
questions.why: Resolution takes the first matching condition, and TS also matches `import`, so it resolves to the `.js` file and finds no sibling declaration. Put `types` first in each conditions object.
questions.asked: Publishing internal packages in a monorepo hits this, and tools like `arethetypeswrong` exist because of it.

questions.q: Why is `b` assignable here, and why does it matter for brands?
choices: Generic types are always assignable when their interface names match
Assignments to a `const` declaration skip type-argument checks
String literal type arguments widen to `string` in interfaces
The unused `T` does not appear in the structure, so it is not compared
questions.why: Compatibility is structural, and `T` contributes nothing to the structure, so `Id<'User'>` and `Id<'Order'>` are identical. A brand must appear in the shape, e.g. `{ value: string; readonly __brand: T }`.
questions.asked: It explains why naive "phantom type" brands do not work, a common mistake when adding nominal IDs.

choices: No: `kind` must be narrowed with a `switch` before the call
Yes: indexing the mapped type keeps `K` and `p` correlated
No: the lookup is a union of functions, so `p` must be an intersection
Yes, but only because `p` is widened to `any` inside the function
questions.why: Because `senders` is typed as a mapped type over `keyof Payloads`, `senders[kind]` is `(p: Payloads[K]) => void`, which matches `p`. Declared as a plain object type, the lookup becomes a union of functions whose parameters intersect and the call fails; this mapped-type pattern (TS 4.6+) is the standard fix.
questions.asked: The "correlated union" problem appears in every typed dispatcher, and knowing the mapped-type fix is a senior signal.

questions.q: In TypeScript 5+, why do NestJS and Angular projects still set `experimentalDecorators: true`?
choices: They rely on legacy semantics, such as parameter decorators
Standard decorators do not run at all without the flag
The flag is required for any class to carry type metadata
It makes decorators run at compile time for speed
questions.why: TS 5.0 implements the standard (TC39) decorators by default, but they have different semantics and no parameter decorators, which constructor injection in Nest and Angular relies on, together with `emitDecoratorMetadata`. The two systems are not interchangeable.
questions.asked: It shows you understand why framework configs differ from plain TS defaults.
